body.para: Converts an expression to the specified data type. CAST is not a statement, but an expression that can be used wherever a value is expected.

CAST ( <eExpression> AS <Type> [(<nWidth> [, <nPrecision>])] [NULL | NOT NULL] )
CAST ( <eExpression> AS ( <cTypeExpression> ) [NULL | NOT NULL] )

<Type>The target type, as a single letter or as a name:
C, CHAR, CHARACTER: Character (padded with spaces to the width)
V, VARCHAR: Varchar (truncated to the width, but not padded)
N, NUM, NUMERIC and F, FLOAT: Numeric and Float
I, INT, INTEGER: Integer
B, DOUBLE: Double
Y, CURRENCY: Currency
D, DATE: Date
T, DATETIME: DateTime
L, LOGICAL: Logical (a string that starts with T or Y gives TRUE, a number gives TRUE when it is not zero)
M, MEMO: Memo
G, GENERAL: General
W, BLOB: Blob
Q, VARBINARY: Varbinary (truncated to the width)
The type is not case sensitive. A runtime error is generated when the expression cannot be converted to the target type.
<nWidth> [, <nPrecision>]The width of the result for character and numeric types and the number of decimals for numeric types. For character values the default width is 1.
<cTypeExpression>An expression between parentheses that returns the type name, for example a variable.
NULL | NOT NULLAccepted for compatibility with the SQL syntax. The clause does not change the result.

? CAST(123.456 AS C(10))
? CAST("42" AS I)
cType := "N"
? CAST("3.14" AS (cType))
